target_customer: HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical and construction businesses
problem: Trade businesses pay thousands per month for leads and then lose many to missed calls and slow follow up.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services, AI phone agent plus outbound and marketing management, with a never-miss-a-lead guarantee
product_category: AI call answering and growth platform for home services

founders.name: Ajith Govind
previous_startups: Turing Labs (YC W20, says it was raising a Series A of over $20M)
founders.background_notes: Education not named on YC page; describes himself as a 2x YC founder with computer science background.

founders.name: Avinash Joshi
previous_startups: Turing Labs (joined Ajith's previous YC startup)
founders.background_notes: Rails programmer per YC page; college batchmate of Ajith.

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents integrated with Housecall Pro, Jobber, FieldEdge and ServiceTitan, plus outbound calling; standard stack with integration and reliability work.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and customer data give some stickiness, but many AI receptionist vendors exist and ServiceTitan bundles its own.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ServiceTitan folded virtual agents into its Contact Center Pro add-on per a vendor guide; no direct action against Cactus found.

market_need_then: YC page and site cite $3K to $25K monthly lead spend and 10 to 20 percent leads lost; the site reports 53K+ calls handled and 90%+ retention, self reported.

identity.mascot_or_character: Spiky the Cactus, shown meditating, peace sign and a caped superhero version; the AI phone agent is named Pam
identity.voice_and_tone: Outcome driven, 'Let AI run your office'

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly mascot and named agent give personality, but the name collides with Cactus Compute and others and no press on the brand was found.

pivots.from: AI assistant for solopreneurs such as private chefs and photographers
pivots.to: AI growth partner for home service trades
pivots.why: Not stated; YC page notes both positionings without explaining the relationship.

outcome_analysis: Cactus narrowed from a general AI assistant to home service trades and raised a reported $7M seed in November 2025 led by Wellington Management and YC, within months of its Spring 2025 batch. Repeat YC founders and reported customer ROI support the story. Competition from receptionist vendors and field service platforms is the main risk.
notes: Seed confirmed by the company press release plus two outlets; the PR date is taken from search coverage as 2025-11-05 but recorded to month. Site also lists Pioneer Fund as a backer, round unknown. Raising.fi shows $1M+ total, conflicting and unverified. Some sources list the batch as X25; YC page says Spring 2025. No competitor sources dated near the batch were found.
